L158:   * cite185†Framework L159:   * cite186†Data L160:   * cite187†Declarative L161: ## Introduction
L162: 
L163: You can start with a React template from Vite and choose "React", otherwise bootstrap your application however you prefer.
L164: 
L165:     `npx create-vite@latest
L166:     `
L167: 
L168: Next install React Router from npm:
L169: 
L170:     `npm i react-router
L171:     `
L172: Finally, render a `<BrowserRouter>` around your application:
L173: 
L174:     `import React from "react";
L175:     import ReactDOM from "react-dom/client";
L176:     import { BrowserRouter } from "react-router";
L177:     import App from "./app";
L178: 
L179:     const root = document.getElementById("root");
L180: 
L181:     ReactDOM.createRoot(root).render(
L182:       <BrowserRouter>
L183:         <App />
L184:       </BrowserRouter>,
L185:     );
L186:     `

L26: # Shared Options cite9†​ L27: 
L28: Unless noted, the options in this section are applied to all dev, build, and preview.
L29: ## root cite10†​ L30: 
L31:   * Type: `string`
L32:   * Default: `process.cwd()`
L33: 
L34: Project root directory (where `index.html` is located). Can be an absolute path, or a path relative to the current working directory.
L35: 
L36: See cite11†Project Root for more details.
L37: ## base cite12†​ L38: 
L39:   * Type: `string`
L40:   * Default: `/`
L41:   * Related: cite13†`server.origin` L42: 
L43: Base public path when served in development or production. Valid values include:
L44: 
L45:   * Absolute URL pathname, e.g. `/foo/`
L46:   * Full URL, e.g. `https://bar.com/foo/` (The origin part won't be used in development so the value is the same as `/foo/`)
L47:   * Empty string or `./` (for embedded deployment)
L48: 
L49: See cite14†Public Base Path for more details.
L50: ## mode cite15†​ L51: 
L52:   * Type: `string`
L53:   * Default: `'development'` for serve, `'production'` for build
L54: 
L55: Specifying this in config will override the default mode for both serve and build. This value can also be overridden via the command line `--mode` option.
